items.title: The top cohomology of a pseudo-coherent complex with bounded cohomology is finite type and finitely presented in the next degree
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma extracts finiteness statements from pseudo-coherence: if a complex K is m-pseudo-coherent and has no cohomology above m, then the module H^m(K) is of finite type, and if it has no cohomology above m+1 then H^{m+1}(K) is finitely presented (statement lines 15964-15974). The proof is a 24-line argument (proof lines 15977-16000) which uses the defining property of pseudo-coherence to replace K by a bounded complex E of finite projective modules agreeing with K in high degrees, and then argues by descending induction on the top degree n of E: when n = m the top cohomology of E is the cokernel of a map from E^{m-1} into E^m, and when n exceeds m the vanishing of H^n lets one split E^{n-1} as a direct sum of E^n and a smaller module E' and repeat. Part (2) then reads the finitely presented module off as a cokernel of a map between two finite projective modules. The splitting step is where the vanishing of the higher cohomology is really consumed, and the reduction to E is what makes the induction possible.
